clue.text: Explodes sculptures, including the head of Rodin

indicators.note: the sculptures take in and hold the other piece inside themselves

parts.note: busts are sculptures of head and shoulders

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: first letter of the sculptor's name

explanation.surface: Someone smashes statues, beginning with the head of a famous Rodin piece.
explanation.walkthrough: Rodin was the French sculptor of The Thinker, which makes the scene of broken sculpture convincing.
explanation.definitionFit: Bursts and explodes are both verbs for blowing apart suddenly under pressure.

clue.text: See 16
Recites aloud instrumental parts?

indicators.note: aloud tells us the word is heard rather than seen, so we want its sound

parts.note: to recite a text is to read it out

explanation.surface: A performer reads out the separate parts of a musical score.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is playful: the vibrating strips in oboes and clarinets are literally parts of instruments.
explanation.definitionFit: Reeds are the thin vibrating strips that produce sound in woodwind instruments such as clarinets and oboes.

clue.text: First to tie knot, went ahead and saw the world

indicators.note: first to a word means its opening letter is the one taken

parts.note: opening letter of tie
a ravel is a tangle or knot
to lead is to go ahead of others

explanation.surface: Someone tied the knot, then set off on a round-the-world honeymoon.
explanation.definitionFit: To have seen the world is to have journeyed widely, which is what a person who has been abroad a lot has done.

clue.text: See 16
Awful mess leaves businessmen scrabbling for some bucks?

indicators.note: awful suggests a disorderly state, so the removed letters may come out in any order
scrabbling is scrambling about frantically, so the remaining letters are jumbled
leaves here means departs from, so those letters go out of the longer word

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, these letters are removed

explanation.surface: Businessmen scramble for a few dollars after leaving an awful mess behind.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove M, E, S, S from anywhere in BUSINESSMEN to leave BUINENS, then rearrange. 'Bucks' looks like dollars, but a buck is also a male rabbit.
explanation.definitionFit: A buck is a male rabbit, and bunnies is a pet name for rabbits, so some bunnies are bucks.

clue.text: Underwear with visible edges — that's audacious

parts.note: a bra is an item of underwear

indicators.note: the edges of a word are its outermost letters at each end

parts.note: first and last letters of visible

explanation.surface: Wearing lingerie with its trim on show is a daring fashion choice.
explanation.definitionFit: Brave and audacious are both adjectives for someone bold enough to take risks without fear.

clue.text: Mob allows production of natural fibre

indicators.note: a production is something made from raw materials, so the letters are worked into a new form

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A crowd permits the making of a natural textile.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambswool is the soft wool shorn from young sheep, an animal-derived textile rather than a synthetic one.

clue.text: Felt testicle, a bit round and complete

indicators.note: turned round means facing the other way, so the piece is read backwards
a bit of the phrase means a piece sitting inside the words

parts.note: letters inside these two words

explanation.surface: A cheeky medical self-examination, feeling for a lump that is roundish.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the join of the first two words and must be read from right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle a bill or a deal is to complete it, finishing the matter by paying or agreeing.

clue.text: Fifty-one pounds held in cash

parts.note: LI is 51 in Roman numerals
quid is British slang for pounds sterling

explanation.surface: Someone has fifty-one pounds tucked away in banknotes.
explanation.walkthrough: A quid is a pound, and the plural is also quid.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquid assets are those kept as money or easily turned into money, unlike property or investments.

clue.text: Process musical work with rocky intro — not right!

indicators.note: rocky means unsteady and shaken, so the letters are tossed into a new order
not right tells us the abbreviation for right is taken away

parts.note: an opera is a sung dramatic work
taken as written
R is the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A musical piece with a shaky opening that is somehow off.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the R from INTRO first, then rearrange the four letters left.
explanation.definitionFit: An operation is a process or procedure, a series of actions carried out to achieve something.

clue.text: Leads in amateur drama may insist theatregoers come clean

indicators.note: the leads of words are those at the front, so each word supplies its opening letter

parts.note: opening letters of five words

explanation.surface: The stars of a village play demand that the audience confess something.
explanation.definitionFit: To come clean is an idiom for confessing, owning up to something one had kept secret.

clue.text: Writer sues miserable publication

parts.note: the writer of a clue refers to themself as I

indicators.note: miserable means wretched and out of sorts, so the letters are knocked out of shape

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An unhappy author takes a wretched magazine to court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miserable publication' reads as one phrase, but 'miserable' works on the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: An issue is one numbered edition of a magazine or newspaper, the thing that is published.

clue.text: Studios for all

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the Hollywood film company and its studios

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition completes the name of the famous film studio; the second is the ordinary adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Universal Studios is a major Hollywood company, and universal as an adjective means applying to every person everywhere.

clue.text: Expressed anger as wanton lodger embraced wife

indicators.note: to embrace is to wrap your arms around, so one piece holds the other inside
wanton means unrestrained and wild, so the letters run riot

parts.note: taken as written
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A husband snarled when a lusty lodger hugged his wife.
explanation.definitionFit: To growl is to make a low angry noise, so someone who growled gave voice to their annoyance.

clue.text: Voting her out within a very short time

indicators.note: out can mean wrong or askew, so the letters are put into a different order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An electorate removed a leader from office almost immediately.
explanation.definitionFit: An overnight success happens suddenly, so the word describes change that arrives with surprising speed.

clue.text: Drunk labourites not able, unfortunately for lover

indicators.note: a drunk person staggers about, so the letters reel into a new order
unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so the removed letters may be taken in any order
not tells us the following letters are missing from the longer word

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, these letters are removed

explanation.surface: Tipsy Labour Party members, sadly incapable, are no use as a partner.
explanation.walkthrough: Take A, B, L, E out of LABOURITES to leave OURITS, then rearrange. Labourites are supporters of Britain's Labour Party.
explanation.definitionFit: A suitor is a man courting a woman, an admirer or wooer, as a lover might be.

clue.text: Compiler's always spending recklessly on champagne hit!

parts.note: the compiler speaking of themself: I am, shortened
forever means always
to blow money is to spend it wastefully
bubbles, or bubbly, is informal for champagne

explanation.surface: The setter confesses to splurging on fizz, then celebrates with a toast.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a 1919 popular song, now famous as the anthem sung by fans of West Ham United football club.
explanation.definitionFit: The song was a successful popular number, and a hit is a record or song that sells well.

clue.text: Extremely literate and eager editorial

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two end letters, taken from each of the next words

parts.note: end letters of literate
end letters of and
end letters of eager

explanation.surface: Praise for a newspaper opinion piece that is highly cultured and enthusiastic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' looks like an intensifier for literate, but it acts on all three following words, even the little 'and'.
explanation.definitionFit: In British newspapers a leader is the editorial article giving the paper's own opinion on a topical matter.

clue.text: Goes back for ringleader fomenting unrest

parts.note: read as ring-leader: the leading letter of ring

indicators.note: fomenting means stirring up, so the letters are stirred into another order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The chief agitator comes back to stir up trouble once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ringleader' reads as one word, but it splits into ring and leader, the opening letter of ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Returns as a verb means comes or goes back to an earlier place, the same sense as the definition.

clue.text: Corrupts sweetheart in rolling fields

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so one piece goes within the other
rolling means tumbling over, so the letters tumble into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
read as sweet-heart: the central letter of sweet

explanation.surface: A romantic picture of a lover out in the rolling countryside, with a darker twist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweetheart' reads as a lover, but it is the heart of sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: To defile is to make impure or spoil something, which is what corrupting it does.

clue.text: Frank, call the shots!

definitions.meaning: second meaning: to be in charge, give the orders

explanation.walkthrough: Frank looks like a man's name being addressed, but it is the adjective for honest speech.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the word means blunt and honest; as a verb it means managing or giving instructions to others.

clue.text: Shylock's first: his job is meagre

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter of the name before it

parts.note: opening letter of the name
Shylock is a moneylender by trade

explanation.surface: A comment on Shakespeare's Shylock: his trade brings in little.
explanation.walkthrough: Shylock is the moneylender in Shakespeare's The Merchant of Venice, so 'his job' points to what he does.
explanation.definitionFit: Slender means small or scanty, as in slender means or a slender chance, just like meagre.

clue.text: Twenties sheet music

definitions.meaning: second meaning: written musical parts for performers

explanation.walkthrough: Twenties suggests the decade or banknotes, but it means sets of twenty.
explanation.definitionFit: A score is an old word for a group of twenty, and also the written notation of a musical composition.

clue.text: Rattle copper, as an example

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Sir Simon Rattle, the British orchestra leader
second meaning: a metal that carries electricity well

explanation.walkthrough: Rattle looks like a verb meaning to shake or unsettle, and copper suggests a police officer; both are examples of the answer. Sir Simon Rattle has led the Berlin Philharmonic and London Symphony Orchestra.
explanation.definitionFit: Simon Rattle directs orchestras with a baton, and copper is a metal that transmits electricity and heat.

clue.text: Say goat lost head

indicators.note: losing its head means the word's opening letter is dropped

parts.note: a goat is an animal that butts, so it is a butter

explanation.surface: An exclamation about a goat that has been decapitated.
explanation.walkthrough: A goat butts with its horns, so in crossword logic it is a 'butter'.
explanation.definitionFit: To utter is to speak or voice words aloud, the same as saying something.

clue.text: Played losing sides for loot

indicators.note: losing its sides means the word's first and last letters are dropped

parts.note: to trifle is to play or toy idly

explanation.surface: A sports team that played badly and lost on all fronts went in search of plunder.
explanation.definitionFit: To rifle a place is to search through it in order to steal, which is what looting means.

clue.text: Transport for Bryan?

parts.note: surface reading: a vehicle laid on for a man called Bryan
setter's reading: a kind of boat that is also the surname of the Roxy Music singer

explanation.walkthrough: Bryan points to the singer who fronted the 1970s band Roxy Music; his surname is a kind of boat carrying passengers across water.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is a boat that carries passengers or vehicles across a stretch of water, and also the singer's surname.

clue.text: Correct pen by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it means we want a word heard the same, not spelt the same

parts.note: to pen a letter is to write it

explanation.surface: A remark that a writing implement seems to be the proper one.
explanation.definitionFit: Right and correct are both adjectives for something accurate and free of error.

clue.text: Got better and renewed insurance

definitions.meaning: second meaning: ..., having taken out cover again

explanation.surface: Someone back on their feet after illness signs up for a fresh health policy.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as RE-COVERED: insurance is called cover in Britain, so renewing it means being covered again.
explanation.definitionFit: To have recovered is to have regained health; split as re-covered it means insured again with a new policy.

clue.text: Uterus repaired with small stitches

indicators.note: something repaired has been put back together, so the letters are rebuilt in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A surgeon closes up a womb after an operation with a few neat stitches.
explanation.definitionFit: Sutures are the stitches surgeons use to close a wound or incision after an operation.

clue.text: Plea for each to let in some light

indicators.note: letting in means admitting something inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: per means for each, as in miles per hour
a ray is a beam, a small amount of light

explanation.surface: A request from everyone that the curtains be opened to brighten the room.
explanation.definitionFit: A prayer is an earnest request or appeal, whether to God or to a person, much like a plea.
